title: Stage 2: metrics
summary: A lookups counter with bounded attributes and a duration histogram whose buckets fit the SLO.

steps.title: What the dashboard needs
body: The on-call dashboard for the bookshop needs: lookups per second split by found / not found, and the lookup latency against
its SLO, "99% of lookups under **50 ms**". So a counter with one bounded attribute, and a histogram in seconds with a bucket

steps.prompt: Which attribute set is right for `app.book.lookups`?
steps.explain: Two series. The id is already on the span, where per-request detail belongs.

steps.title: Count and time the lookups
prompt: Keep stage 1 and add, with a `Meter` named **`Bookshop`** registered through `.WithMetrics(...)`:
- histogram **`app.book.lookup.duration`** (unit `s`) of the handler's time in seconds, no attributes, with boundaries exactly
starter: var found = books.TryGetValue(id, out var title);
return found ? Results.Ok(new { id, title }) : Results.NotFound();

public static readonly ActivitySource Source = new("Bookshop");
public static readonly Meter Meter = new("Bookshop");
public static readonly Counter<long> Lookups = Meter.CreateCounter<long>("app.book.lookups", unit: "{lookup}");
public static readonly Histogram<double> Duration = Meter.CreateHistogram<double>("app.book.lookup.duration", unit: "s");
hints: Add `.WithMetrics(m => m.AddMeter("Bookshop").AddView(...))` to the builder and two instruments to `Telemetry`.
template: public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
foreach (var id in new[] { 1, 2, 9, 3, 1 }) await http.GetAsync($"/books/{id}");
var span = await DojoOtel.Span(a => a.DisplayName == "load book");
Dojo.Check("stage 1 still holds", span is not null, "");
